Commentary.Commentary: So that is it from us for this game! Sri Lanka win a pulsating Test match and avoid embarrassment by chasing down a mammoth total. Zimbabwe showed great character to take it down to the last day. The batting performance will give the Lankans great confidence heading into the Test series against India. The action will begin between the two Asian sides on 26th July. Zimbabwe on the other hand will head back home and work on their skills as they are not playing cricket for quite a while. We look forward to your company in future. Till then, take care and cheers!

Sri Lanka skipper, Dinesh Chandimal says that it has been a really good Test match. Credits his players as they have worked really hard. Mentions that it is tough to bat on day 5 and adds that the batsmen needed to apply themselves. Feels happy that the batsmen did just that. Gives a special mention to Gunaratne and Dickwella for batting so well. States that as a captain you have to be responsible on and off the field. Declares that it is a tough challenge for them against India but he is confident of a good show from his boys.

Zimbabwe skipper, Graeme Cremer says it is a little disappointing. Credits Sri Lanka for chasing a big target on day 5. Appreciates Rangana Herath for picking wickets at regular intervals. Mentions he is proud of his boys for fighting it out and taking it to the last day. Admits that the ODI series was a high point for them and it gave them the belief to compete in this Test match. Ends by saying that they have had a very good time in Sri Lanka and he hopes they will come back soon to play another series.

Man of the Series, Rangana Herath says that he's aware that he has bowled more than 23,000 balls in First Class cricket. Mentions that he enjoys playing cricket and wants to bowl more in future. States that it is good to go past the records of Marshall and Botham in the all time bowling list. Opines that it was a good game. Feels that Raza was playing a lot of sweeps and reverse sweeps and made it difficult for them. Adds that it was a challenge and they took it. Ends by saying that he is looking forward to the big series against India.
Man of the Match, Asela Gunaratne says he is extremely happy for what he has done. Thanks the team and the support staff for their support. Ends by saying that he is very happy that the team won.

Zimbabwe in both the innings were rescued by the lower order batters. That's a big positive for them. Sri Lanka have to be credited for achieving a come-from-behind victory, especially after conceding the psychological advantage at the end of the first innings by trailing Zimbabwe by 10 runs. The batters' efforts in the second innings had to be lauded as they didn't crumble under the pressure of a mountain of runs required.

The Zimbabweans can take heart from the fact that even though they were the lesser ranked side among the two, they were the side that was on top for most part of the game. Graeme Cremer, the skipper, was brilliant with the ball, claiming 9 wickets in the match. He was really probing the Sri Lankan batsmen with his guile. There were some half chances and some missed opportunities that, if grabbed, could have resulted in the match having a different end. All in all, this match proved to be yet another reason as to why Test cricket is alive and kicking.

So! It all comes to an end in the way it actually should have! Sri Lanka win and what an innings to finish it off by Asela Gunaratne. He kept his calm and played his shots and also cleverly rotated the strike to see off the tense moments in the last two sessions, ably supported in that last unbeaten 67-run stand, by Dilruwan Perera. Let's not forget the important innings that Niroshan Dickwella played, which acted as a catalyst for the run chase. Dinesh Chandimal, the new Sri Lankan skipper is elated with this victory and why not. This was the fifth highest successful chase in Tests.

Zimbabwe bowlers in this session had many ooohs and aaahs as there were edges that fell away from the fielders and also quite a few plays and misses. There's still a lot on offer for the bowlers, and they have to ensure that they keep up the pressure and bowl in good areas. Sri Lanka require 118 more runs to win, while the African visitors need to snap up 5 wickets for a brave victory; which side will take it all? Join us for the exciting action after lunch.

But then Dickwella and Gunaratne got in and have consolidated well so far. The former has used the sweep shot to great effect and has accumulated runs steadily, reducing the deficit in the process. Remember, he got a big let off from the third umpire when he was on 37.

Loopy ball on leg and spinning away from the batsman, Asela defends it on the leg side.

Starts the over with a slow ball outside off, Asela goes on the back foot and defends on the off side.
Back of length ball on off, Niroshan plays it towards the off side off the back foot. Mpofu begins with a maiden.
Back of length ball pitching outside off and coming into Dickwella, he defends it off the back foot.
Full delivery outside off, Niroshan defends it outside off.

Chris Mpofu into the attack. Pace for the first time in this innings.
50-run stand between Dickwella and Gunaratne.

Sean Williams into the attack.
Flatter ball in the line of the stumps, AG plays it towards the mid-wicket. No run there.
Loopy ball on middle, Dickwella plays it towards long on for a single.
Now Gunaratne sweeps it towards square leg for a single. That was a flighted ball on off stump.

The third umpire looks at numerous replays and rules that in the batsman's favour. Dickwella's back leg was on the line with nothing behind, it appeared. But he has been given the benefit of doubt. The whole of the Zimbabwe team and the dressing room look flabbergasted! They just can't believe it, but the play has to carry on.
There is a stumping appeal against Niroshan Dickwella which has been taken upstairs. Chakabva seems to be very confident.
Flighted ball on middle, ND paddles it away again for a couple towards fine leg.
This time Niroshan paddles it towards fine leg for a couple. It was flighted on middle and off.

FOUR! Raza is being targeted by the Lankans here. That's a good flighted ball on off, Dickwella gets down on one knee and sweeps it through mid-wicket for a boundary. That's a wonderful shot, and ND looking very confident today.

That was bowled outside off, Dickwella plays it towards point for a single.
Loopy ball on off, Gunaratne flicks it through square leg for a run.

Starts round the wicket and gives the ball some air on middle and leg, Gunaratne defends.

Loopy ball outside off, Dickwella opens the face of the bat and guides it towards third man for a single.

Loopy ball on off and middle to welcome Gunaratne which he defends.
The harmstrung Asela Gunaratne walks in next.

OUT! Gone! Cremer traps the big fish Mathews. Well, well. Sri Lanka crumbling away here. Bowls a googly on off, inviting a drive. Shortish ball on off, Mathews plays it off the back foot towards covers.
Shortish ball on off, Mathews cuts it to the right of the point fielder. No run.

Floats it outside off, gets some extra bounce on that. Dickwella tries to play the sweep but gets beaten. Replays show that the ball hit the grill of the helmet of the keeper. Thankfully he was wearing a helmet or that would have hit him on the face.
Tosses it on off, Dickwella defends it off the front foot.
Mid on drops back a bit.

Fires it in on leg stump, Mathews flicks it towards fine leg for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

That was the googly which Dickwella didn't seem to pick up. He wanted to play it on the leg side but the ball spun away, hit his thighs and rolled away towards slip.

The players are out in the middle. It is a cloudy morning in Colombo as the overnight Sri Lankan batsmen Mendis and Mathews walk out to resume their innings. Graeme Cremer is seen giving a huge pep talk to the team on this vital day for them. Sean Williams to start with the ball, with a slip and a short leg.

PITCH REPORT - Alistair Campbell and Dean Jones feel it is one of the best 5th day pitches they have seen. Opine if they can keep Cremer under 3 wickets Sri Lanka can win. Reckon it is still a good wicket and partnerships will be the key.

Zimbabwe on the other hand have a chance to create history. They have only bowled with their spinners so far and are starting to get a lot of assistance from the surface. A lot will depend on their captain Graeme Cremer who is spinning the ball square and having a jolly time with the ball. We are certain to have a result unless the weather intervenes. We are in for an exciting day of cricket.

Hello and welcome to the final day of the one and only Test between Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe. We have had four pulsating days of cricket and the visitors find themselves slightly ahead. Chasing a mammoth target, the home side has their best batsmen in the form of Angelo Mathews and Kusal Mendis battling out and they would hope they do the bulk of the scoring.
...Day 5, Session 1...

Scores in excess of 300 have been chased only thrice on the Sri Lankan soil. The hosts will need to bat really well to brave past the tourists. Can Zimbabwe create history by registering their first victory in Tests against Sri Lanka or will the home side prove their mettle? Join us for the final day tomorrow at 1000 local (0430 GMT). Till then, cheers!

Kusal Mendis is cramping up but he is fighting it out for the cause of his side. He is unbeaten on 60 and getting good support from Angelo Mathews. The good thing is that the home side has kept the scoreboard ticking and are still in the hunt. Earlier in the day, the lower middle and tail of the visitors did extremely well to set a steep target of 388 for the hosts. Afterwards, their bowlers came out and made life difficult for the opposition.

Another absorbing day of Test match cricket! The Sri Lankan batsmen have battled it out in the middle but Zimbabwe are slightly ahead at the moment. The rough areas have opened up more and the spinners are extracting good bite from it. Cremer once again bowled with great control to pick up two wickets while Williams bowled a jaffa to bamboozle Karunaratne.

...Day 4, Session 3...
The over rate from Zimbabwe has been excellent and with only 30 overs remaining, we might see more getting bowled today. We are in for an exciting last session. Join us in a while.

Sri Lanka have negotiated the period before tea really well. They have managed to add 56 runs in 18 overs and have not lost a wicket. Tharanga and Karunaratne have looked solid in the middle. Zimbabwe have only bowled with their spinners so far and they have started to get a little purchase out of the surface.
